key_insight: Frontier LLMs gave very different triage advice for possible stroke symptoms, and their recommendations changed a lot based on wording and context.
clinical_relevance: Because stroke care is time-critical, inconsistent model advice could delay emergency evaluation when people ask an AI for help with neurological symptoms.
method: Benchmarked 3 LLMs: Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT-4o, and Llama 3.3-70b-versatile.
Tested first-person stroke-like vignettes across 10 symptom descriptors, 2 phases, and with/without a distractor.
Ran 50 prompts per condition to compare triage responses.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong cross-model and framing effects, including post-exam divergence and a distractor-associated drop in emergency-care recommendations.
watch_item: These results come from scripted vignette testing, so real-world performance may differ and the findings should not be treated as clinical guidance.
paper_title: Cross-Model Variability in Large Language Model Triage Behavior for Potential Stroke Symptoms
